label: original-phase inputs b/f/h/d/3 (boosted by earlier m/t/w/z)
explanation: Fires almost only while the original tokens are being read (98% of mass in phase 0). It never fires at t=0 and seldom at t=1, and the rate rises with position. It is nearly silent at the delimiter and during the copy phase. The current input token gives the strongest signal: b, f, h, d and digit 3 have 3.3-4.3x lift and hold about 66% of the mass. Weaker inputs are c, q, r, e, u and y. Activation also seems to build up from earlier tokens: sequences that start with or contain m, t, w or z (first_tok m 3.2x, prev2_tok m 2.6x) fire more often and more strongly, and the top examples are b/f inputs after an m/t/w/z prefix. It fires mostly on the first occurrence of a token (in_first gives 1.6x vs 0.3x). It looks like a graded sum of input-token and prefix evidence rather than a clean rule. The token-set predicate reaches only about 0.5 F1. Adding the prefix condition raises precision to 0.66 but loses recall. Widening the token set gets 0.89 mass recall at 0.32 precision.
